summary: The Raiders beat the Jets 16-12 on NBC's "Sunday Night Football" in a defense-heavy game with only six field goals through three quarters. Michael Mayer's leaping end-zone catch 50 seconds into the fourth quarter gave Las Vegas the first touchdown, and Robert Spillane's late interception of Zach Wilson sealed it. The win moved interim coach Antonio Pierce to 2-0 and into the AFC playoff race, while the Jets went a second straight game without a touchdown.
one_line: The Raiders held off the Jets 16-12 on Sunday Night Football, scoring the game's only touchdown in the fourth quarter and sealing it with a late interception.
key_facts: The Raiders beat the Jets 16-12 on Sunday, Nov. 12, 2023, at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas; kickoff was 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC.

The game had only six field goals through three quarters; the first touchdown came 50 seconds into the fourth quarter on a leaping end-zone catch by Michael Mayer from Aidan O'Connell, putting the Raiders up 16-9.
Zach Wilson went 23-for-39 for 263 yards, no touchdowns and an interception, and rushed four times for 54 yards.
Aidan O'Connell completed 16-of-27 passes for 153 yards, a touchdown and an interception.
Josh Jacobs had season-best marks with 27 carries for 116 yards, while Breece Hall and Dalvin Cook combined for just 17 rushes for 54 yards.
Robert Spillane intercepted Zach Wilson's pass intended for Allen Lazard with 1:14 left, returning it to the Raiders' 40.

Jacobs lost a fumble at the Jets' 25 in the fourth quarter, forced by Jamien Sherwood and recovered by Ashtyn Davis, but the Jets failed to score a touchdown after it and had to settle for a field goal.
The win made interim coach Antonio Pierce 2-0 since the firing of Josh McDaniels and put the Raiders among five AFC wild-card contenders with at least five wins.
The Jets went a second straight game without a touchdown and have lost two in a row before facing the Bills in Week 11.
The Jets were repeatedly hurt by penalties, with six for 68 yards by the third quarter, including holding calls on C.J. Uzomah that wiped out a Hall touchdown run.
Aaron Rodgers did not play, despite the preseason expectation of an Aaron Rodgers vs. Jimmy Garoppolo matchup.
Daniel Carlson kicked a 54-yard field goal at the end of the first half, and Greg Zuerlein made all of the Jets' field goals.
NBC's broadcast crew was Mike Tirico on play-by-play, Cris Collinsworth on commentary and Melissa Stark on the sidelines.
